stories.summary: Add Bat Color Selection UI for HSV Detection Configuration

details.user_story: As a user, I want to select my bat color before uploading a swing video, so that the AI service can accurately detect and track my specific bat type without requiring manual HSV configuration.
details.context: DM-33 implemented color-based bat tracking using HSV ranges configured via environment variables on the server. This requires manual configuration and doesn't allow users to specify their bat color. To improve usability, we need a UI component that lets users select their bat color (black, red, blue, silver, wood) before upload, which will send the appropriate HSV ranges to the AI service for processing.
acceptance_criteria: Bat color selector UI appears before video upload (on empty state screen)
Predefined color options: Black, Red, Blue, Silver, Wood (Brown)
HSV ranges are sent to AI service as part of upload request
Backend passes HSV parameters to AI service during video processing
Default selection is 'Black' (most common aluminum bat color)
Color selection persists during app session but resets on app restart
UI is accessible and follows app design language
technical_details: Mobile App Changes (App.js):
- Add batColor state variable (default: 'black')
- Create bat color selector component in upload card
- Display color options as chips/buttons with icons
- Pass batColor to UploadService.uploadSwingVideo()
Mobile App Changes (UploadService.js):
- Accept batColor parameter in uploadSwingVideo()
- Convert bat color to HSV ranges using preset mapping
- HSV_PRESETS object with black, red, blue, silver, wood mappings
- Send HSV ranges as query parameters or request body to backend
Backend Changes (main.py):
- Update /api/videos/upload endpoint to accept HSV parameters
- Accept bat_hsv_lower and bat_hsv_upper as optional parameters
- Pass HSV values to AI service in the multipart request or as headers
- Maintain backward compatibility (use defaults if not provided)
AI Service Changes (main.py):
- Update /analyze/pose endpoint to accept HSV parameters
- Accept bat_hsv_lower and bat_hsv_upper from request
- Pass HSV values to PoseExtractor.process_video()
- Override environment variable defaults with request parameters
AI Service Changes (pose_engine.py):
- Update process_video() to accept optional bat_hsv_lower and bat_hsv_upper parameters
- Use provided HSV ranges instead of global BAT_HSV_LOWER/BAT_HSV_UPPER
- Maintain backward compatibility with environment variables
UI Design:
- Color selector appears below 'Analyze a Swing' text in upload card
- Horizontal scrollable row of color chips
- Each chip shows: bat icon + color name + color indicator dot
- Selected chip has accent border and background tint
- Compact design (doesn't overwhelm the upload card)
edge_cases: Invalid HSV Values: Backend should validate HSV ranges are within [0-180] for H, [0-255] for S/V
Network Failure During Upload: Bat color selection should be retained if user retries upload
Multiple Bat Colors in Video: User must select dominant/primary bat color (future: support multiple selections)
Custom Colors: Future enhancement - allow users to create custom HSV ranges via sliders
Accessibility: Color chips should have text labels, not just color indicators, for colorblind users
Backward Compatibility: AI service should still work with old mobile app versions that don't send HSV parameters
